# Architectural rules, with what enforces each

<!-- generated by scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs -- do not edit -->

> Generated from `workflow.ai.yml` by `node scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs`. `AGENTS.md` carries the first
> sentence of each; this file carries all of it and what fails when it is broken.

- The core is framework-agnostic. Nothing under src/Core, src/Workflow/Model, src/Workflow/Graph, src/Workflow/State or src/Mesh may import or name a Symfony class, and those directories import upward into nothing but themselves and src/Core. Symfony lives at the edges: the parser (Yaml), the runners (Process, HttpClient), the console, the event dispatcher bridge. A change that needs an exception belongs in infrastructure, behind an interface the domain owns.
  *Enforced by:* `tests/Unit/Architecture/BoundaryTest.php` (token scan of the pure directories), reviewed under dimension 1
- PHPStan runs at level 9 with zero errors and no ignoreErrors: not in phpstan.neon, not as a baseline file, not as an inline @phpstan-ignore comment. A type the analyser cannot follow is fixed in the code, with a precise docblock, a value object or an assertion at the boundary, never silenced.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (phpstan.neon and inline ignores), `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the level), and CI (Verify on PHP 8.4 and 8.5)
- The engine is deterministic. Given the same workflow, the same runner outputs and the same injected clock and id source, a run takes the same steps in the same order and ends in the same state. Decision logic under src/Core, src/Workflow and src/Mesh reads no wall clock, no randomness and no environment: time arrives as a Psr Clock, ids as an injected generator, configuration as constructor arguments. DAG ordering breaks ties by declaration order, never by hash order.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (determinism rules for those directories); tie-breaking and replay by review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 2)
- Retry-loop isolation. When a step fails and on_failure retries a target, the next prompt receives only the isolated failure of the last attempt (the stderr or the failing assertion), never the accumulated error history. The retry count is bounded by max_retries, and a bounded exhaustion ends in the declared escalation, not another loop.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 2); the engine's retry tests under tests/Unit/Workflow are the evidence a review asks for
- One runner contract. Every way of running an agent or a command implements RunnerInterface and returns a RunResult; the engine, the mesh and the console depend on the interface and the registry, never on a concrete runner. A runner owns its process or connection, honours the timeout and cancellation in its RunRequest, reports token usage when it knows it, and never leaks a child process.
  *Enforced by:* `tests/Unit/Architecture/BoundaryTest.php` (only the registry's composition code may name a concrete runner); the contract itself by review (dimension 2)
- Secrets are never logged. API keys and tokens reach a runner through the environment of its own process or its own Authorization header and nowhere else: not in a trace attribute, an event, an exception message, a result artifact, a prompt or a log line. Every outgoing representation of a request redacts them.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (credential shapes in source, committed .env files, a heuristic for logging a credential); redaction behaviour by review (dimension 4)
- No shell string interpolation of untrusted data. Processes are started with an argument array through Symfony Process. The only code that may hand a string to a shell is the runner for commands the workflow author declared (ShellRunner), and nothing derived from a model's output, a file name, a branch name or an artifact path is concatenated into a command line. eval, the shell functions, the backtick operator, unserialize of untrusted data and the @ operator are banned everywhere.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (banned constructs, the fromShellCommandline allowlist); the data flow into ShellRunner by review (dimension 4)
- Paths are confined. A path taken from a workflow file, a model, a guard or an artifact name is resolved against its root and rejected if it leaves it, before it is read, written, diffed or handed to git. Worktrees live under .indaba/worktrees/&lt;taskId&gt; and nowhere else, and teardown removes only what the manager created.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 4); the confinement tests named in the owning spec
- Observability follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. A task is a trace, a workflow step a span, an LLM call, a tool execution or a shell verification a child span, with gen_ai.* attribute names for the system, the model and the input and output token counts, and cost as a separate, documented attribute. The conventions are still developing; the attribute set in use is recorded in the observability spec, and a rename follows the convention, not taste.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 5); the span and attribute tests of the observability feature
- Every feature has a specs/&lt;feature-name&gt;/ directory containing spec.md, api-surface.md and review.md. Each of plan.md, tasks.md, data-model.md, research.md and events.md is either written or named in spec.md under Artifacts not written, with the reason it does not apply.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/check-workflow.mjs`; the track check holds a feature commit to it (`scripts/check-track.mjs`)
- Runtime dependencies are a recorded decision. composer.json require lists exactly the packages project.runtime_dependencies names, every Symfony component on one constraint, and composer audit is clean. A new entry requires the decision in the feature's spec, because every one is a version Indaba can force onto a consumer's tree.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the list and the Symfony constraint) and CI (Dependency audit)
- Public API changes are classified before they are written. Adding a class, an optional constructor argument with a default or a method is a minor; changing a signature, a default, an enum case, the workflow file schema, a CLI option or an emitted event or span attribute is a major. Record the classification in the spec and in CHANGELOG.md. Below 1.0 a major takes the next minor and says so.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 3)
- PHP runs in Docker. The host has no PHP 8.4, and a result from any other interpreter is not evidence. Every PHP command in this repository, in a hook, in documentation and in a report, is docker compose run --rm php composer &lt;script&gt; or the equivalent vendor/bin call inside it.
  *Enforced by:* review; the pre-commit hook and CI both run composer qa, so a change that only works on another PHP fails in CI
- Repository documentation moves with the change: AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and specs/DEPENDENCY_MAP.md whenever the public surface, the architecture or the release contents change, and the files under docs/ in the same change as any added, removed or changed workflow field, guard, runner option, CLI option or default.
  *Enforced by:* review (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
- No invented numbers. A token count, a cost or a duration that Indaba reports was measured or received from the provider, or is labelled an estimate with its source (the pricing table's date). A cost is never silently zero because a model is missing from the table: unknown is reported as unknown.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 5)
